newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Volkswagen denies Asian chief to step down.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen denies Asian chief to step down.

text.p: Germany's biggest carmaker, Volkswagen AG on Sunday denied a magazine report that its management board member with responsibility for Asia, Martin Posth, was planning to step down at the end of November.
"Posth has no intention nor is he planning to step down," a Volkswagen AG spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Hong Kong.
According to an article released in advance from Monday's Der Spiegel, Posth was planning not to ask for an extension to his contract at the supervisory board meeting on November 29.
The magazine said that Posth had been forced to hand over responsibility for sales and marketing in Japan to the management board member responsible for sales, Robert Buechelhofer.
Spiegel said further that Posth had been criticised because of problems at the group's China plant.

Volkswagen said that the handover to Buechelhofer came about because the Japanese business had developed into a normal export business, whereas Posth's responsibilities in Asia lay in developing Volkswagen production in the region.
The spokesman said it was local conditions in China, including smuggling and grey imports, which had affected sales at the local production plant.
Also orders had been affected during the summer of this year as people had been waiting for the passing of a new five-year plan by the Chinese government.
